title: Matthews brothers and Depression pick-up bands
summary: Brief talk of the Matthews brothers, then Foster lists places he played in pick-up bands as bands broke up in the Depression.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Do you remember much about Frank Matthew? Frank Matthew? Yeah. He led a band at the Tivoli in Mexico with Charlie Love, Deucin.
Frank Goody. No, I don't know him. I know Bibb Matthews, Bill Matthews.
These guys are all brothers. All brothers, yeah.
I think there's a bunch of, come on, Bill Matthews, Bibb Matthews, and Freeman. I think they got another one, I can't call his name.
Yeah, another younger one, I think didn't take up music they told me.
Yeah, that's the one I can't call his name.

Bill Matthews played drums for the funeral the other day. For the funeral, yeah, for Barbaran's funeral. Just at Barbaran's funeral, yeah. I'm surprised he hadn't played drums for many years, he said.
Oh yeah, it's been quite a while since he played.

And on trombone all the time. Trombone. Are there any other jobs that you can think of during the Depression that you had that lasted any time at all? I guess most of them were just a few nights at a time, but any special bands that you played with?
Well, it was most get together bands.

I played up at Black Gold, Seven and Howard. I played out there for Miss Normandale, St. Mary and Constance. I played at Paradise and Philly and Rampart. I thought it was anybody higher, you know. Yeah, bands commenced to breaking up like that. Which I left the Depression got over, but then the bands started to making up again.
